comment: PoC dev config: file-system storage.
Story 7.1: custom CredentialsExtractor unions the REAL Solid-OIDC token path
(DPoP + Bearer, from css:config/ldp/authentication/dpop-bearer.json) WITH the
debug UnsecureWebIdExtractor (Authorization: WebID <uri>, from debug-auth-header.json).
Both auth base configs define urn:solid-server:default:CredentialsExtractor, so they
cannot both be imported; this restates the combined waterfall in one definition instead.
Why both are needed: real backoffice users (Epic 7) authenticate via OIDC and were getting
a blanket 401 on every write/.acl request because debug-auth-header alone dropped the DPoP
extractor entirely. The ~15 internal automation files (pipeline/, agents/) still rely on the
WebID header via the Docker-internal CSS_CONNECT_URL path.
SECURITY: UnsecureWebIdExtractor trusts Authorization: WebID <uri> with no verification.
That header is stripped at the nginx-gateway edge for all public traffic (Story 4.4.1,
04-pocpod0.conf), so it is only reachable from inside the Docker network. DO NOT remove
that edge stripping. DO NOT USE this debug extractor on a server exposed without it.
Story 7.13: CSS's own identity pages (main.html.ejs, Story 7.2 restyle) load
tokens.css from pod.nicolasdb.eu's root. That used to be served for free by the
backoffice's StaticAssetHandler block (also mapped '/tokens.css'), which was
removed in Story 7.13's origin split — breaking this page's styling as a side
effect. tokens.css is CSS's own dependency now, kept as its own copy here
(infra/css/tokens.css) rather than reaching into backoffice/, which CSS no
longer has bind-mount access to at all post-7.13.
